reviewerStance: I did not author the subject and I owe it nothing. I am not bound by the v1.7 reviewer's opinions, and this review tests its guidance rather than merely checking that the guidance was followed.

verdict.summary: B-R17-01 IS REPAIRED. All three original repairs are independently recomputed and correct, all five operations apply at zero errors, and every structural claim v1.8 makes about itself -- 0 digests moved, 5 sets / 0 adds / 0 removes, no design decision changed, still NOT shippable as production finding identity -- is verified TRUE. The blockers are not against the repair; they are against the NEW surface v1.8 added in discharging G-2. The derived class of self-measurements does not do what it is offered as doing: its published size is unrecomputable by construction, it misses the artifact's own designated self-report block almost entirely, and the limitation it discloses against itself is FALSE in its load-bearing clause. One newly authored self-measurement is false of the value it will bind.
verdict.wouldClearWith: B-R18-01 and B-R18-03 are each a small, mechanical edit. B-R18-02 requires changing the derivation BASIS, not widening the pattern -- see advisory A-R18-02.
verdict.scoredBy: FINDING-SET DELTA against the resolved value. No exit code was consulted; no checker was executed.

resolutionDiscipline.rule: freeze 7.3 / CMP-IR-01 -- a derivation must be RESOLVED, not read flat. This corpus has committed the flat-read error five times, twice on the day of this review.

resolutionDiscipline.deliveredBytesNotAuthoringIntermediate: CONFIRMED. v1.8 derives from 30810d73..., which is the v1.7 file on disk. It is not 242d80f8..., the authoring intermediate the original v1.7 review bound. v1.8 states this and it measures true.

RESOLVED, the identifier is present at two leaves. Had I read flat I would have raised a false finding that v1.8 dropped an open-dependency disclosure -- the identical mistake that produced the withdrawn A-7.

freeze 7.2.2's rider names precisely this shape: gates that 'run at write time, once, in a process nobody can re-execute', so that 'a reviewer can verify the properties they produced; it cannot verify that they ran'. The freeze grades this WEAK EVIDENCE. It does not grade it a standing recompute obligation.

v1.8 does not delete the figure, does not soften it and does not claim it verified. It retains it as provenance, states plainly that it must NOT be handed to a reviewer as a recompute task, and names the concrete remedy: 'emit the 47 strings, or their digests, as data in the artifact'. That remedy is correct and sufficient.
The direction of the change is toward LESS claimed assurance, which is the honest direction. An evasion would move the other way.

blockers.finding: v1.8 publishes 59 as a DERIVED figure and states its method. The method turns on 'a numeral or a WORD-numeral'. No word-numeral vocabulary is published, and the 59 members are not enumerated anywhere in the artifact -- only 5 repaired and 5 named unaffected. Neither the method nor the extension permits the hard comparison 7.2.2 requires.

blockers.whyThisIsABlockerAndNotAnAdvisory: The freeze AT THE PINNED DIGEST 6e0d36a6... records this exact defect being caught and repaired ONE DAY BEFORE v1.8 was authored, in the very section v1.8 cites as its authority for counting word-numerals. Section 7.2.2: 'VOCABULARY PUBLISHED 2026-08-11, because this table committed its own section's defect. An independent reviewer reported it could reproduce the integer halves exactly and neither word figure -- the counts were published under an unpublished vocabulary, so they were not recomputable, which is precisely what 7.2.2 forbids.' And its rule, verbatim: 'A figure without its definition is not a measurement, however true it is.' The freeze even records the corrective act and praises the artifact that took it for 'publishing its own 41-token vocabulary in full'. v1.8 publishes none.
blockers.notAClaimThat59IsWrong: I am not asserting 59 is arithmetically false. I am asserting it is UNCHECKABLE, which under 7.2.2 is the finding. My 62-70 range is evidence of non-reproducibility, not proof of miscount.
blockers.repair: Publish the word-numeral vocabulary as a closed token list, and publish the extension -- the 59 member paths -- so the figure can be hard-compared. Both are mechanical.

theDisclosedLimitationIsFalse.rule: freeze 7.2.2.1 -- the vacuous caveat. A DISCLOSED LIMITATION can be false; reviewers hunt overclaims and pass over concessions. Recompute limitations, not just claims.
theDisclosedLimitationIsFalse.v18Text: 'Freeze 7.2.2's retention-tiers.v26 case is exactly a defective leaf whose key -- recordedInputs -- ends in nothing the key pattern would catch. The prose fallback mitigates that. Whether it CLOSES it is not measured, and a reviewer should assume it does not.'
theDisclosedLimitationIsFalse.clause1_theRetentionTiersDiagnosis: TRUE. Verified: the key pattern does not match 'recordedInputs'. v1.8 names the right case.
theDisclosedLimitationIsFalse.clause2_theProseFallbackMitigatesThat: MEASURED FALSE. Across the ENTIRE resolved value the prose fallback rescues exactly 6 leaves, and 0 of them are self-measurements -- they are contract prose (fieldSetRule.theHonestStatement, primitives.text.ruleAsApplied, a declaredDepartures note) and three encoder error strings from rejectionControls. It rescues 0 leaves in $.measuredSelfReport. Worse, it is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of the case it claims to mitigate: the fallback requires /longest|widest|headroom|across all|text component|bound is/ to match the VALUE, and the retention-tiers.v26 shape is a BARE NUMERAL ('15' where the bytes held 19). A bare numeral carries no prose, so the fallback can never fire on it. Mitigation is not merely unmeasured -- it is impossible.
theDisclosedLimitationIsFalse.clause3_aReviewerShouldAssumeItDoesNot: Honest and correct, but it is guarding a sentence that is false rather than merely unproven. The concession understates a systemic 88% miss rate in the designated self-report block as an edge case.

It is a bare-numeral self-measurement, so v1.8's own derived class would not catch it either. B-R18-02 and B-R18-03 are the same failure seen from two sides.

The 8 is diagnostic colour supporting a correct repair, not the repair itself.

advisories.title: Operation 5's regrade is right but scope-incomplete, and partial labelling creates a false contrast
advisories.finding: The regrade is applied to rawByteStringsHashedOutsidePython = '47', the one leaf in the block that carries no assurance weight. Its siblings mismatches = '0' and mismatchExamples = [] have IDENTICAL epistemic status -- the same unre-executable authoring process, the same moment, no artefact to recompute against -- and mismatches = 0 is the leaf a reader actually relies on, since the block's whole stated purpose is a cross-implementation check (hashlib versus shasum(1)). After operation 5, one leaf in the block is explicitly labelled UNVERIFIABLE AUTHORING ATTESTATION and its siblings are not. A reader will reasonably infer the unlabelled siblings ARE verifiable. In aggregate the block is now less honest than before the repair, which inverts the operation's intent.
advisories.notABlockerBecause: The direction is toward less claimed assurance, the labelled statement is true, and the named remedy would fix all three leaves at once.
advisories.repair: Label the shasumCrossCheck BLOCK rather than one leaf, or take the remedy operation 5 already names -- emit the 47 strings or their digests as data -- which discharges 47, mismatches and mismatchExamples together and converts the whole block from attestation to evidence.

advisories.title: G-2, the prior reviewer's guidance, was under-specified, and v1.8's faithful execution of it is what produced B-R18-02. I do not endorse G-2 as written.
advisories.testingTheGuidanceNotTheCompliance: The dispatch asked whether the guidance was RIGHT, not merely whether it was followed. It was followed. It was not sufficient.
advisories.finding: 'Derive the class, do not patch rows' is correct in principle and fixes the ENUMERATION mode (hand-listed versus derived). It does not say derive it BY WHAT. v1.8 chose key name -- the single basis this corpus has recorded as broken most often: CMP-IR-01 itself; the retention-tiers.v26 'recordedInputs' case; and freeze 7.3, which explicitly REPLACED name-based detection with VALUE-SHAPE detection 'precisely because locating a declaration by name reproduces the defect'. Fixing ENUMERATION with an instrument vulnerable to SCOPING trades one of the freeze's four named modes for another.
recommendedBasisForASuccessor: PRIMARY, by value shape: every leaf whose value is a bare numeral, or a numeral-plus-unit or numeral-plus-qualifier string ('44 of 44 enumerated', '9 -- NOT EXTENDED'), or a digest. This catches duplicateKeysFound, componentFrameOccurrencesInEP8, framingGate.assertions and every measuredSelfReport leaf B-R18-02 lists.
SECONDARY, by structural position: every leaf beneath the artifact's declared self-report blocks -- measuredSelfReport, parseDiscipline, primitives.framingGate -- regardless of key or value.
KEY NAME used only to ADD members, never to BOUND the class.
Publish the extension, not only the cardinality, so the class itself can be hard-compared (this also discharges B-R18-01).
advisories.note: Under that basis the class is materially larger than 59. The right successor move is a bigger, published, shape-derived class -- not a wider regex, which freeze 7.2.2 already records as 'does not close the class'.

onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.instruction: Test whether the guidance was RIGHT, not merely whether it was followed.
onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.G-1_repairTheReasonNotOnlyTheNumber: RIGHT, and discharged. This was the sharpest thing in the v1.7 review. The false reason ('the width of a Digest') was the actual defect; the number was its symptom.
onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.G-2_deriveTheClassDoNotPatchRows: RIGHT IN PRINCIPLE, UNDER-SPECIFIED IN PRACTICE, and its execution is the source of two of my three blockers. See A-R18-02. The guidance named the mode to fix (ENUMERATION) without constraining the basis, and the basis chosen reintroduces SCOPING.
onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.G-3_expressTheDerivedDependency: RIGHT, and discharged well. Stating 79 = 8 + 71 with a named re-derivation obligation is strictly better than stating 79, and would have prevented B-R17-01 had it been present in v1.7.
onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.G-4_foldInTheRelatedAdvisories: RIGHT. v1.8's decision to record A-7's raising AND withdrawal in full is correct and I endorse the stated reason: 'a withdrawn finding that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from one never raised.' Its account is independently verified above.
onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.G-5_thisIsANewByteState: RIGHT, and observed. This review binds d53aa31d... and nothing else.
onTheV17ReviewsGuidance.netAssessment: Four of five items of guidance were right and are discharged. The fifth was right in aim and wrong in the freedom it left, and v1.8 fell into that freedom rather than through any carelessness. The prior reviewer's own stated non-checks were, as the dispatch suggested, its most useful output.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not verify that the 5 findingId values are the CORRECT digests of their canonical tuples. I measured WIDTH (79) and COUNT (5 distinct, 13 occurrences) only. Whether finding:sha256:f4d9aba7... is the true FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 of its ruleId/ruleMajor/stabilityClass/subject/anchor tuple is a design-level recomputation I did not perform. It was reviewed at v1.7 and v1.8 moves no digest, but it is NOT re-earned by this review.

I did not recompute any of the 209 digest-valued leaves against their preimages. I compared them across resolved v1.7 and resolved v1.8 for MOVEMENT only. 'digestsMoved: 0' is verified as NO DIGEST CHANGED, never as ALL DIGESTS ARE CORRECT.

I did not verify whyNoDigestMoves ('None of the five leaves is an input to any preimage') by tracing the preimage grammar. I verified the observable CONSEQUENCE -- no digest changed -- which is consistent with the mechanism but does not prove it. A leaf could be a preimage input and still leave digests unmoved if its own repair were compensated elsewhere; I did not rule that out.

I did not execute check-r1-v1.7.py or any other corpus checker against anything, including as a sanity control.
